item.title: Tennessee’s Andy Ogles Faces Well-Funded Opposition in House Primary Thursday
item.description: Representative Andy Ogles received President Trump’s endorsement, but his challenger, Charlie Hatcher, a former state agriculture commissioner, has the backing of Gov. Bill Lee.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei, Tim Balk and Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: George Walker IV/Associated Press; Kenny Holston/The New York Times
item.media:description: Charlie Hatcher, left, a former state commissioner of agriculture, was endorsed by Gov. Bill Lee on Tuesday. Andy Ogles, a two-term congressman, has the endorsement of President Trump.

item.title: Moderate Democrats Prepare for ‘War’ Against an Ascendant Left
item.description: One moderate group says the progressive wins are “deeply troubling” and is planning a $15 million effort against democratic socialism.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: After a closer than expected election night, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed won his primary contest against a more moderate candidate.

item.title: A Growing Number of Election Deniers Hold Key Local Roles in Midterms
item.description: These officials oversee or help administer elections in counties across the nation where competitive House and Senate races will determine control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Nick Corasaniti and Alexandra Berzon
item.media:credit: Eric Lee/The New York Times
item.media:description: A surge of election deniers hold key offices overseeing or helping administer state and local elections, according to data from the Voting Rights Lab and a Times analysis.

item.title: Senate Panel Has Obtained Copy of Fauci’s Cellphone
item.description: The development comes as a Senate committee prepares to vote Thursday on whether to hold Dr. Anthony S. Fauci in contempt of Congress for refusing to answer questions at a hearing.

item.media:description: A Senate committee Thursday is set to vote on whether to hold Dr. Anthony S. Fauci in contempt of Congress for refusing to answer questions.

item.title: F.D.A. Approves Moderna’s mRNA Flu Vaccine
item.description: The agency had initially refused to even review the application but reversed course after a public outcry.
item.dc:creator: Christina Jewett
item.media:credit: Bill Sikes/Associated Press
item.media:description: Moderna has said that the faster new approach used to prepare the vaccine will enable a shift away from the current process of focusing on one flu strain for an entire hemisphere each season and allow each nation to pick its best option.

item.title: Federal Judge Weakens The National Firearms Act
item.description: The National Firearms Act mandated a permitting process for short-barreled rifles and shotguns, as well as suppressors. A judge ruled that the provision was unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.category: Brady Campaign to Prevent Gun Violence
Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives
item.media:credit: Carlos Barria/Reuters
item.media:description: A visitor points to firearms at an exhibition booth during the National Rifle Association’s annual meeting and exhibit in Houston this year. The two lower rifles are outfitted with suppressors.

item.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York said that Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s close victory in the Michigan Senate primary put “working-class Americans back at the heart of our politics.”
item.dc:creator: Jeffery C. Mays
item.media:credit: Vincent Alban for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York last month at Gracie Mansion in Manhattan. Mr. Mamdani was asked on Wednesday about similarities between him and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, who won Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary.

item.title: Fauci Faces Contempt of Congress Vote on Thursday

item.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
item.description: The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.
item.dc:creator: Adam Entous
item.media:credit: Todd Heisler/The New York Times
item.media:description: Havana in 2019. The C.I.A.’s action coincides with stepped-up efforts by U.S. intelligence agencies to get a better understanding of the situation on the ground inside Cuba.

item.title: Helicopter Carrying Trump Flew Near Passenger Jet in Washington Airspace
item.description: Marine One, the helicopter that ferries the president, came within less than a mile of an Envoy Air flight on Tuesday, raising new concerns about air traffic control in the congested area.
item.dc:creator: Kate Kelly
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: Marine One, right, carrying President Trump, flying to Joint Base Andrews on Tuesday.

item.title: Bunny Dolls and Disturbing Allegations: Max Miller’s Strange CNN Interview

item.media:description: Representative Max Miller was interviewed live on CNN about his allegations on Tuesday.

item.title: After Michigan Loss, AIPAC Weighs a Second Effort to Defeat El-Sayed
item.description: The pro-Israel organization spent $32 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It might try again in the general election.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: AIPAC’s super PAC spent $32 million to boost the opponent of Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in the primary.

item.title: Scandal Leaves North Carolina G.O.P. With No Candidate and Little Time
item.description: Representative Chuck Edwards’s decision to drop his re-election bid amid sexual harassment charges came as a Democratic farmer, Jamie Ager, was already making inroads.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Medina
item.media:credit: Mike Belleme for The New York Times
item.media:description: Representative Chuck Edwards, Republican of North Carolina, dropped his re-election bid just over 12 weeks before Election Day.

item.title: Francesca Hong Said Thanksgiving Should Be Canceled. Can Wisconsin Voters Forgive Her?
item.description: “Cancel Thanksgiving,” she wrote. “VDay” brings out “the worst of humanity,” she mused. Francesca Hong’s old social media posts get a fresh look ahead of Wisconsin’s Democratic primary for governor.

item.media:credit: Joshua Lott/Getty Images
item.media:description: Francesca Hong has struggled to explain past stances on social media with the primary approaching.

item.title: Trump-Backed Michigan Candidate Loses Primary to Rival Who Suspended His Campaign
item.description: Without running a single ad or filing a campaign finance report, Tom Smith, who had suspended his bid, soundly defeated Amir Hassan, a Navy veteran backed by President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Paul Sancya/Associated Press; Tom Smith for Congress
item.media:description: Amir Hassan, left, had hoped to take on Representative Kristen McDonald Rivet, a first-term Democrat in Michigan, but the Republican nomination went to Tom Smith, right, who had suspended his campaign.

item.title: Why Polling Overestimated Abdul El-Sayed’s Advantage in Michigan

item.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall

item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed greeting the audience at his election watch party in Detroit.

item.title: Trump Seeks a Boost for Hemp That Would Benefit a Top Aide’s Family
item.description: At the White House’s request, senators tucked a change sought by the hemp industry into a crucial spending bill. It would benefit the son-in-law of Susie Wiles, the president’s chief of staff.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth P. Vogel, Christina Jewett and Olivia Diaz
item.media:credit: Antranik Tavitian for The New York Times
item.media:description: Intoxicating hemp, which is less regulated than marijuana and alcohol, has gained popularity in recent years as a pain reliever and an alternative to other intoxicants.

item.title: Takeaways From the Primary Elections in Michigan
item.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed narrowly prevailed over Representative Haley Stevens in the Democratic primary for Senate in Michigan, setting up a nervy race to November for the party.

item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s close primary victory signaled that he has work to do to unite Democrats and turn out swing voters in November.

item.title: Shri Thanedar Is Ousted by a Democratic Socialist in a Michigan House Primary
item.description: Representative Shri Thanedar is among a wave of Democratic incumbents in Congress whom primary voters have sent packing in a surge of anti-incumbent fervor this cycle.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed Wins Democratic Senate Primary in Michigan in a Victory for the Left
item.description: Dr. El-Sayed, a progressive former public health official, narrowly defeated Representative Haley Stevens, a moderate, in a bitter primary dominated by the politics of Israel.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed pushed Israel to the center of the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, criticizing the country’s actions in Gaza and promising to pull back American military support.
